what.title: What is dustic?
what.body: dustic is a minimalist audio player that streams music, audiobooks, podcasts, and other audio content from your own sources, the Internet Archive and FunkWhale. Browse millions of free audio recordings, from live concerts to historical radio programs, all in a clean, modern interface.

pwa.title: Install as an App
pwa.intro: dustic is a **Progressive Web App (PWA)**, which means you can install it on your device and use it like a native app. Once installed, it works offline for your saved content and provides a full-screen experience without browser UI.
pwa.introAfter: , which means you can install it on your device and use it like a native app. Once installed, it works offline for your saved content and provides a full-screen experience without browser UI.
pwa.ios1: Open dustic in Safari (not Chrome or other browsers)
pwa.ios2: Tap the Share button (square with arrow pointing up)
pwa.ios3: Scroll down and tap "Add to Home Screen"
pwa.android2: Tap the menu (three dots) in the top-right corner
pwa.android3: Tap "Add to Home screen" or "Install app"
pwa.outro: After installation, dustic will appear on your home screen with its icon and can be launched like any other app on your device.

sources.title: Audio Sources
sources.iaBodyAfter: (archive.org) is a non-profit digital library offering free access to millions of historical and cultural artifacts, including live concerts, audiobooks, podcasts, and radio programs.
sources.fwBodyAfter: is a decentralized, community-driven music platform. You can connect to public FunkWhale instances in Settings to search and stream their music libraries alongside Internet Archive content.
sources.footer: dustic does not host any audio files. It provides a unified interface to discover and play content from these sources.

disclaimer.title: Content Disclaimer
disclaimer.body: All content available through dustic is served directly from the Internet Archive and connected FunkWhale instances. The creator of dustic is not responsible for the content, accuracy, or availability of any audio files or metadata provided by these sources.

privacy.title: Privacy & Data Collection
privacy.intro: **No data collection.** dustic does not collect, transmit, or store any personal information on external servers. Your listening activity is completely private.
privacy.introRest: dustic does not collect, transmit, or store any personal information on external servers. Your listening activity is completely private.
privacy.storage: All your data (favorites, playlists, listening history, and settings) is stored locally in your browser's cache using localStorage. This means:
privacy.point1: Your data never leaves your device
privacy.outroRest: To keep the app simple and privacy-focused, there is no cloud infrastructure or account system to sync profiles between devices. However, you can export and import your profile using the buttons in Settings → Profile Data to transfer your data between devices.

backup.title: Important: Backup Your Profile
backup.intro: While your data is automatically saved in your browser's cache, it can be lost if you:
backup.point1: Clear your browser's cache or data
backup.strong: We strongly recommend downloading your profile regularly to avoid losing your favorites, playlists, and listening history.
backup.outro: You can download and upload your profile using the buttons in the sidebar's Profile Manager section.

openSource.title: Open Source
openSource.body: dustic is open source software. You can view the source code, report issues, or contribute to the project on GitHub.

support.title: Support & Feedback
support.footer: If you enjoy dustic, consider sponsoring the project. Report bugs or suggest features via GitHub issues.

audio.title: Audio Quality
audio.description: Choose the audio quality for streaming and downloads.
audio.scopeNote: Applies to Internet Archive only — FunkWhale and your folders use whatever the file provides.

lowest.label: Lowest Quality
lowest.description: Smallest file sizes. Best for mobile data or slow connections. Formats: 64kbps MP3, 128kbps MP3, Ogg Vorbis.

medium.label: Medium Quality (Recommended)
medium.description: Good balance of quality and size. Formats: VBR MP3, 128kbps MP3, Ogg Vorbis.

best.label: Best Quality
best.description: Highest quality available. Larger file sizes. Formats: FLAC (lossless), 320kbps MP3, VBR MP3.

note.body: Quality applies to both streaming and offline downloads. Not all items have all formats available - the app will use the best match.

libraries.intro: Choose where your audio comes from: the Internet Archive's public catalogue, one or more FunkWhale servers, and/or your own cloud folders.
libraries.iaSubtitle: Millions of free recordings: live concerts, vinyl rips, old radio, audiobooks…
libraries.fwSubtitle: Federated music communities. Add one or more public instances.
libraries.foldersSubtitle: Play your own audio — music, audiobooks, courses — from a cloud folder you already use. Works with Koofr, Nextcloud, pCloud (paid plan), or any cloud that supports WebDAV.
libraries.nicknamePlaceholder: e.g. My audiobooks, koofr, History course
libraries.urlHelp: Get this from your cloud provider's settings. Common examples in Help below.
libraries.rootPathHelp: The folder inside your cloud that holds your audio. Leave as "/" to browse everything.
libraries.errExplain: 401 = bad username/password, or your provider requires an app-specific password (see Help below). 404 = the URL or root folder doesn't exist.
libraries.helpKoofr2: Username = your Koofr email. Password = an app-specific password generated in Koofr → Account → Preferences → Password → App passwords.
libraries.helpNextcloud2: Username + password from your Nextcloud account. App password recommended if 2FA is on.
libraries.helpPCloud1: pCloud (paid plan only): https://webdav.pcloud.com/ (US) or https://ewebdav.pcloud.com/ (EU). Username = pCloud email. Password = your pCloud password (if 2FA is on, you must use an app-specific password from pCloud → Settings → Security → App passwords).

autoplay.subtitle: Configure how dustic chooses the next track when the queue is empty

autoplay.contentTypesHint: Which kinds of audio autoplay is allowed to pull in. Music-only by default to avoid Internet Archive's podcast-heavy popularity charts.
autoplay.contentTypesMinOne: At least one type must stay enabled.
autoplay.sourcesHint: Where autoplay is allowed to pull random tracks from. Toggles for sources you haven't configured (no FunkWhale instances, no WebDAV libraries) have no effect.
autoplay.sourcesMinOne: At least one source must stay enabled.
autoplay.how2: Higher weights = more likely to be used
autoplay.how3: Multiple rules can be enabled at once
autoplay.how4: Rules are tried in weighted random order
autoplay.how5: If a rule fails, the next one is tried
